reason: The narrative demonstrates agency among multiple non-leaders throughout the passage. The Israelites collectively exercise agency by moving and camping (וַיִּסְע֖וּ בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל). The people of Moab collectively exhibit agency through fear and distress (וַיָּגָר מוֹאָ֜ב, וַיָּ֣קָץ מוֹאָ֔ב). Most strikingly, Balaam's donkey—a non-human, non-leader entity—demonstrates independent agency by perceiving the angel of God, responding to danger, and influencing Balaam's path through its own actions (וַתֵּ֣רֶא הָאָתוֹן֩ אֶת־ מַלְאַ֨ךְ יְהוָ֜ה). Even Balaam's servants lack the agency to perceive what the donkey perceives. The text explicitly attributes independent will and perception to non-leadership figures.
